questions.stem: A fleet model has a binary buy[v] per van and a continuous miles[v] between 0 and 40,000. The rule: a van that is not bought drives 0 miles. Which call states it?

options.says: The indicator must be a binary; miles[v] is continuous, and MathOpt refuses such an indicator at solve time with INVALID_ARGUMENT.
The indicator must be a binary; miles[v] is continuous, so the call is refused whichever value activates it.
Right: the existing binary is the indicator, activate_on_zero=True makes the row hold when the van is not bought, and with miles[v] >= 0 the one-sided row means 0 miles.
Without activate_on_zero the row holds when buy[v] = 1, so every van bought would be forced to drive 0 miles.

origin.section: Any Binary in the Model Can Be the Indicator

questions.stem: A program holds ic, an indicator constraint z = 1 implies load <= 300, and a scenario needs the limit at 250. What does the program do?

options.text: Delete ic and add the rule again with 250, keeping the new object
options.says: Right: indicator constraints can be deleted, not edited, and the old object refers to a deleted constraint afterwards.

options.text: Assign ic.upper_bound = 250, as one does for any linear row of the model
options.says: IndicatorConstraint properties have no setters; the assignment raises an AttributeError (lesson 4.3.1 shows it).

options.text: Add a linear row load <= 250 next to ic, keeping both of them in place
options.says: A plain row holds whatever z is, so it forces load <= 250 even when the rule is off.

options.text: Delete ic and leave the rule out, since an indicator constraint cannot change
options.says: The rule is still wanted at 250: delete ic and add it again with the new limit, keeping the new reference.

origin.section: An Indicator Constraint Reads Back, but Cannot Be Edited

questions.stem: A team's service solves every model with HiGHS through MathOpt 9.15. A modeler wants an implication whose switched quantity has a known bound of 900. What should the model contain?

options.text: An indicator constraint, since HiGHS turns it into a row with M = 900 by itself
options.says: HiGHS refuses the model outright: 'Highs does not support indicator constraints'.

options.text: An indicator constraint with the bound of 900, sent through CP-SAT instead
options.says: Through MathOpt 9.15, CP-SAT refuses indicator constraints too (UNIMPLEMENTED); its native form is only in its own API.

options.text: An indicator constraint, with the exception caught so the solve goes on
options.says: Catching the exception gives no plan at all; the model still has no solver that takes it.

options.text: A linear row with M = 900, since HiGHS takes linear rows
options.says: Right: with a known bound the linear row is exact and runs on HiGHS, as the reserve rule showed with the same NPV.

origin.section: The Solver Decides Whether It Accepts Indicators, and the Reason Is on `__context__`
